C’est par un jeudi après-midi que nous r: We meet the restaurant’s founder on a Thursday afternoon in the Rivière-des-Prairies neighbourhood. It is 3 p.m., the neighbourhood is peaceful, and spring is settling in.
À l’intérieur du comptoir gourmand, quel: Inside the eatery, a few regulars are seated at their tables, enjoying their meals. The walls, adorned with paintings, make the space an unusual place.
Dans cette atmosphère accueillante, le j: In this welcoming atmosphere, the slender young man joins us to share his journey. His sleeves always rolled up, Ramzi sits up straight. Propriétaire du restaurant depuis l’âge: The owner of the restaurant since the age of 19, Ramzi did not have his parents’ financial help, nor did he follow the traditional academic path to success.
« Je savais que le système de l'école n': “I knew that the school system wasn’t – unfortunately or fortunately – made for me,” he says with a shrug. “I didn’t want to go to CEGEP or to university.”
Très jeune, il a un rapport difficile av: From a very young age, he had a difficult relationship with school, where he struggled to thrive. Rather than diligently following his classes, he preferred to have fun and quickly became the class clown.
« Ça m’a coûté cher puisque j’ai redoubl: “It cost me, because I repeated a year twice,” he lets slip. The young man nevertheless believes that the experience shaped him and pushed him to explore other paths. “I matured, and then I found the one that suited me better: entrepreneurship,” he concludes, his fist clenched.
« Tout ce que je fais pour moi, je le fa: “Everything I do for myself, I also do for my parents”
En secondaire cinq, après un cours de fi: In Secondary 5, after a finance class on retirement, Ramzi went home and brought up the subject with his parents. His mother, a civil servant at the time, confided that she hadn’t managed to prepare properly for that stage of life. The young man couldn’t believe it.
« On nous a toujours enseigné qu'il fall: “We’ve always been taught that you have to study for years, get a good job, contribute to a pension fund for forty years so that you can finally rest!” he exclaims. “But seeing the reality of retirement for my parents, I knew it wasn’t the path I wanted to follow.”
Ramzi a alors deux objectifs en tête : s: Ramzi then had two goals in mind: to secure his financial future without taking the traditional path of education, while also guaranteeing his parents’ financial security for the years to come. “It’s a race against the clock,” he says, tapping his wrist with his index finger. “They’re nearing retirement and I want to make sure everything goes well for them.”
D’un même souffle, il poursuit : « On n': In the same breath, he continues: “We never really talked about it, but we’ve already been through losing our home. That’s what pushes me to fight today, to avoid going through that nightmare again. What I do for myself, I also do for my parents,” he adds, before casting an embarrassed glance.
« Même si on a peu, en réalité, on a bea: “Even if we have little, in reality, we have a lot”
« Mes parents m'ont appris à être heureu: “My parents taught me to be happy with what I have. Even if we have little, in reality, we have a lot,” he says, a smile in the corners of his eyes.
Ramzi lives this mantra to the fullest.
Durant la pandémie, le jeune homme trava: During the pandemic, the young man worked full time at Home Depot. “The atmosphere at home was strange. I was working full time, my mother too. We were tired of our jobs, my father was off work for the first time even though he’s a hard worker, and my brother was doing school at home, a situation he hated. I was desperately looking for solutions,” he explains.
En mai 2020, alors que les restaurants s: In May 2020, while restaurants were closed because of health restrictions, an idea struck him like lightning: selling smoothies through Snapchat. “One day, I opened my fridge and noticed a smoothie. I closed it and told myself: ‘I’m going to sell smoothies tomorrow,’” he tells us, raising his head toward the ceiling. He continues: “My mother was right next to me, she looked at me and said: ‘Okay, tomorrow we’re going to the wholesaler.’”
Le lendemain, le 20 mai 2020 à 17 heures: The next day, May 20, 2020, at 5 p.m. sharp, he specifies, the Smoothzi adventure began in the family kitchen. “Mom made the doughnuts, Dad the crêpes and me the smoothies,” he says, slicing the air with his hands to punctuate each task. “The photos of the prototypes were taken, the ad was posted, and in an hour and a half everything was sold,” he concludes proudly.
Le soutien inconditionnel de sa mère, Sa: The unconditional support of his mother, Sabiha Merabet, is inspiring. She wears a sober grey sweater, which contrasts with her son’s printed one. Her short-cropped hair adds an elegant touch to her appearance.
D’un timbre de voix également plus calme: In a calmer tone of voice as well, she says: “Ramzi has always supported me, he has always believed in me. When he told me about his project, it was completely natural to come on board with him, to accompany him and to support him. I believe in him, and I also believe in the strength of young people and in their vision.”
Sabiha a brièvement travaillé dans le se: Sabiha briefly worked in the restaurant industry in 2014. That experience gave her knowledge that she now wants to pass on to her son.
Alors qu’elle travaille à temps plein à: While working full time at the Rivière-des-Prairies prison, she, and then the whole family, followed Ramzi on this adventure. From May to December, every day after work, between 7 p.m. and midnight, the family business came to life in the kitchen.
Une expérience qui a rapproché la famill: It was an experience that brought the family closer: “Before, we never saw each other, everyone was in their own room. Now we see each other all the time. There’s no better gift for me than being with my parents all the time, and I think it’s a great gift for them too,” says Ramzi, his eyes sparkling.
« Quand les restaurants ont rouvert en 2: “When restaurants reopened in 2020, I thought I was going to stop everything. I told myself I had accomplished my mission, which was to replace restaurants at that time,” Ramzi confides.
Cependant, il envisage la suite autremen: However, he saw the future differently when he realized that the demand came directly from the people in his neighbourhood. “Friends would come and tell me: ‘So where am I going to order my smoothies now?’”
Ramzi décide alors de se remettre au tra: Ramzi then decided to get back to work. “During my two weeks off from Home Depot, my father and I started working together from 8 a.m. to 11 p.m. to develop different recipes.” It was a conclusive experiment, the young man says: on the very first day, he was able to sell smoothies worth the equivalent of a week of his salary. “That’s when we told ourselves that we could open a restaurant and take the risk of really making it work!”
Dès l’ouverture de l’établissement en dé: From the day the restaurant opened in December 2020, Ramzi received considerable support from the residents of Rivière-des-Prairies, who flocked to discover his sweet and savoury counter.
« Une des raisons pour laquelle on a ouv: “One of the reasons we opened our first restaurant in Rivière-des-Prairies was to show consideration for the Montréal-Nord community. We wanted to serve them, give them a warm, friendly place, and show consideration for young people,” he says with conviction.
À l’intérieur de l’établissement, on tro: Inside the restaurant, there are a few gifts given to congratulate him: a pair of AF1 sneakers printed with Smoothzi, as well as a guest book signed by customers since 2020.
« Beaucoup d[‘entre eux] appellent mes p: “Many of [them] call my parents ‘Dad and Mom.’ As a son, when I see [that], it’s mission accomplished, it means they truly feel cared about,” he says, beaming.
Au-delà de cette considération affective: Beyond this emotional bond, Ramzi is also committed to the Rivière-des-Prairies community by offering a space for emerging artists. “This place isn’t just a restaurant. We host art openings for artists and offer a stage for artistic performances.”
Le jeune homme de 23 ans a un message d’: The 23-year-old has a message of hope for his generation: “You have to believe in yourself, nothing is impossible! Of course it’s not easy, but all the hardships are worth it. Because the point of a trial is to learn to overcome it.”
Sabiha est du même avis : « Les projets: Sabiha shares this view: “Projects we undertake that don’t come to fruition aren’t failures, they’re experiences,” she says, referring to her first experience in the restaurant industry, which didn’t work out but is useful today to the family business.
Ces mots, empreints de sagesse, incarnen: These words, steeped in wisdom, embody the spirit of hope and determination that drives Ramzi’s family.
